versions.changelog: Bounded context recovery and durable handoffs; preserve human blockers across retries, overflow and terminal acceptance; explicit checkpoint chronology and generated-dispatcher regressions.
Exactly-once queue execution, crash-safe recovery, project relay and installer fixes, and dashboard gate security hardening.
Opt-in backlog status reconciliation with fail-closed project and task-binding safeguards; deferred internal relay routing.
Release 0.15.20: opt-in project backlog relay with fail-closed authority and duplicate-enqueue safeguards.
Recover dispatcher launches rejected during OpenClaw Gateway restart drain; match only explicit non-zero restart signatures and avoid unrelated 503 or successful-output replay.
Recover interrupted OpenClaw turns via runtime session rotation while preventing successful recovered turns or quoted prompts from being replayed; add regression coverage.
Fix OpenClaw doctor and disposable smoke compatibility with strict account validation by removing the synthetic doctor account while preserving real source-account forwarding.
Resolve nested checkpoint project identity; defer future authorization gates while safe work remains; strengthen regression coverage and synchronize packaged version docs.

Lock accepted task terminals against broader-project scope creep; require authoritative source/actor/generation-bound Gate artifacts; fail closed for empty or unbound gates and suppress actionable dry-run commands.
Add authoritative cross-interface Human Gates, quota runtime decisions, durable multi-agent team controls, and updated OpenClaw verification guidance.
Add the project-first operator workspace, Gateway-coupled Dashboard autostart, and fail-closed localhost/Tailnet listening modes.
Fix public CI setup for repositories without an npm lockfile.
Add transactional state kernel, public Goal API and five-command CLI, public CI, and seven competitive acceptance fixtures.
Fix human-gate materialization so only explicitly missing, currently needed authority blocks progress; honor standing production authorization and checkpoint-bound project backlogs.
Clarify OpenClaw smoke write scope and require checkpoint evidence; add regression coverage.
Preserve and deduplicate non-blocking terminal checkpoint risks in final judgement summaries, including accepted project completions, with regression coverage.

Prevent accepted phase checkpoints from being misjudged as terminal completion; preserve continuation risks; use accepted terminal contracts as completion authority; reconcile stale post-completion gates into done.
Support external-only authoritative project backlogs in project-status, fail closed when no backlog source exists, and avoid false registry drift when no embedded projection is configured.
Prevent future paid/deploy/publish gates from stopping safe local backlog work; automatically reconcile premature waiting gates; recover incomplete embedded-runtime turns.
Preserve source conversation routing across revisions; fail closed on unroutable routed revisions; materialize the newest authoritative blocked project human gate; add end-to-end regression coverage.

Remove workspace-specific Ironman queue/dispatcher instructions; resolve each machine's installed queue and managed wrapper; add regression coverage against host-specific dispatcher leakage. Existing queue data is untouched.
Improve terminal notifications with final judgement and checkpoint summaries, enforce Chinese queue localization, and link notification ledger evidence back to run artifacts.
Fix OpenClaw and Hermes scheduler health reporting when asynchronous notification delivery fails.

Reconcile project-scoped human gates with authoritative contracts and acceptance ledgers; strengthen project status and doctor drift checks; make supersession project-aware; add durable gate regression coverage.

Add the platform-neutral runtime adapter SDK v1 for OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, with shared conformance tests, fail-closed effects, redacted telemetry, migration guidance, and a credential-free demo.
Add production-trust runtime adapters, durable journal/replay, safe upgrade planning, multi-agent soak/canary tooling, and detached acceptance refresh.
P0-P3 release: Human-Gate Lifecycle v2, action idempotency and reservations, multi-agent typed todo control plane, and read-only Operator Dashboard.
Add English/Chinese installation adaptation, complete English conversation routing semantics, fail-closed delivery metadata checks, and notification-backed terminal delivery.
Add Hermes Agent install, doctor, smoke, source-bound delivery, managed scheduler, and fail-closed platform confirmation summaries for both OpenClaw and Hermes.

Clarify upgrade intent: product-level Loop Engineering upgrades now mean the complete managed Skill, npm/CLI, OpenClaw integration/queue, and scheduler lifecycle by default; only explicit Skill-only requests remain limited to ClawHub content, with per-layer verification required.

Reclaim orphaned dead-PID queue locks; preserve non-sensitive human attestations while keeping secrets one-time; prevent historical gate resurrection; support normal requeue from superseded waiting gates.
Fix durable checkpoint recency and blocked human-gate reconciliation; prevent legacy cp9 reviews from overriding blocked cp46+ checkpoints and move blocked tasks into waiting_for_human.
Recover compaction and transport interruptions with bounded fresh-session resume; proactively rotate long project sessions; install the recovery policy through managed OpenClaw upgrades.
Automatically install, enable, verify, upgrade, and uninstall the managed per-queue scheduler so project loops cannot remain queued indefinitely.
Project-aware completion and checkpoint lineage; durable redacted human gates; orphan active-task recovery; fail-closed scheduler heartbeat health checks.
Preserve explicit human acceptance gates, fail closed on missing delivery routing, and complete tasks only after approval.
Add official npm/GitHub installation details and complete OpenClaw integration verification commands so a standalone ClawHub skill can bootstrap the CLI.

Rename Loop Engineering to Taskforce Loop Engineering while preserving the established task/project loop workflow, immediate execution semantics, amendment and supersede handling, and strict project completion contracts.
